Script-only reading: every line works on its own. In 01-3, 'the rest' refers back to the 01-2 list of paperwork, set against time with patients. In 02-2, 'here' points to the laptop and the WELBUK PRACTICE label in 02-1. In 02-3, Meera's opening 'And' continues Ananya's 02-2 line directly, with no removed speech in between. In 03-2, 'Of course' answers Ravi's 03-1 request. In 03-3, 'Yes, please' answers the 03-2 consent question. In 03-4, Meera can use Ravi's name because she has just registered him. In 04-2, Ravi answers the 04-1 question, and 'your concerns' in 04-4 refers back to 04-2. In 05-2, Ravi's 'So...' follows from 05-1 plus the screen he is looking at, and 05-3's 'That's the idea' answers him. In 06-1, 'Tomorrow ... may' frames what follows as hypothetical.

Source comparison: every lettered source string appears verbatim and in source order. No question has lost its answer. No pronoun is left without its referent. No turns from different speakers are merged. The only split is Meera's single 01-2 source line, broken at the ellipsis into two balloons by the same speaker. The order is unchanged and no other speaker comes between them, so I accept it. The added captions are WELBUK PRACTICE/CARE/HEALTH role labels on 02-1, 02-3 and 05-2, plus a second WELBUK VISION label on 06-3. The source's own panel descriptions support them, and coverage records them as additions.

Speaker voice matches the source. Ananya is calm and leads ('Let's...', 'One team.', 'We'll ... together'). Meera is polite and capable ('Of course. May I...', 'That's the idea.'). Ravi is warm and plain-spoken ('Good morning!', 'Yes, please.').

Cause and effect: paperwork pressure (01-2) leads to Ananya's resolve (01-3), then onboarding with Practice and Care (page 2), consent-based registration (page 3), an unhurried human consultation (page 4), Health for staying connected after the visit (page 5), and the conditional vision (page 6). How Welbuk was chosen is never shown, but the source omits it too. That is acceptable for a six-page onboarding comic.

The three product roles are distinct. Practice is for the clinic (02-1 label, Ananya at the laptop, 'organise our clinic workflow'). Care is for staff (02-3 label, Meera on a staff phone, 'each staff role'). Health is for patients (05-1 line, 05-2 label, Ravi's own phone). 06-4 repeats all three in the source's order.

Future vision is kept separate from current features. 06-1 is conditional ('may'). 06-2 and 06-3 each carry a 'WELBUK VISION' label, sit inside a pale-blue vignette with a lighter palette (style.continuity and the vision section), and 06-2 also says 'The vision:'. 06-4 returns to the present ('vignette disappears') and its captions make no feature claim. The specialist, partner and child appear only inside the vignette, and their appearances are recorded as manga supplements.

Medical and data safety: 'feeling tired lately' is a routine concern, 04-4 gives no treatment, and 04-4 bans prescriptions and instruments. The consultation room bans text-bearing charts. The monitor and phone screens are abstract or blank, the 03-3 monitor shows blank fields, and no ID cards or written papers appear. 05-3 keeps 'what is available to you' and the 05-2 screen is described as conceptual, so no unlaunched live feature is claimed.

Previous issue (phone props), checked independently and resolved. In the request, section reception.objects now defines only 'ravi-phone' ('Ravi's own smartphone (dark blue case)'), and no 'patient-phone' remains anywhere in the script. 05-1: the scene says Ravi 'holds his own smartphone (dark blue case) in his right hand'; production.before is 'took out his own phone'; prop ravi-phone goes before 'in Ravi's pocket', during 'in Ravi's right hand', heldBy ravi.right, which matches hands.ravi.right. 05-2: held in both hands, before 'in Ravi's right hand', after 'held by Ravi', and production.after 'Ravi keeps his phone'. 05-3: held by Ravi off-panel, heldBy none, which fits because he is outside the frame. 05-4: before 'in his hand after the walkthrough', during 'in his left hand', heldBy ravi.left, which matches hands.ravi.left and the scene. 06-1: before 'in his hand', during 'in his lap', heldBy ravi.left, which matches hands and scene. The chain now runs through one object with no contradiction, and the 05-2 'So I can keep...' reads naturally as Ravi looking at his own phone.

Minor non-blocking continuity notes for later stages (artwork-dependent). (a) 05-2 lists heldBy 'ravi.right' while hands and 'during' say both hands; the field can hold only one hand, so this is consistent. (b) Ravi's shoulder-bag, present in 03-1, 03-3 and 03-4, is not recorded in 04-1 to 05-4; the art should keep it visible (on his shoulder, lap or chair) or the storyboard should note where it is. (c) In 06-4, Ravi's left hand is empty and no phone is recorded; acceptable because it is a symbolic present-day closing portrait separate from the 06-1 train scene. (d) 01-2 has Meera voicing her wish while holding the receiver mid-call; that is plausible as a sigh aside, but her expression and gesture must make it read as said to herself. (e) 05-2's 'So...' depends on the conceptual screen visibly suggesting appointment and info cards. None of these blocks the script.

Transitions without source captions (02-4 to 03-1 later morning, 04-4 to 05-1 back to reception, 06-3 to 06-4 return to the present) rely on the art. The transition fields record the visual bridges, and this must be confirmed at storyboard and artwork.

panels.observation: Caption 'A busy day at Dr. Ananya's clinic.' matches source P1-1 verbatim. It is the opening line, depends on nothing earlier, and names Ananya before she speaks in 01-3. The scene keeps the source's morning Tamil Nadu clinic and 'Dr. Ananya welcomes patients'.

Source P1-2 has one Meera line, 'Appointments, patient details, follow-ups... I wish everything were easier to manage!'. The script splits it at the ellipsis into two Meera balloons, same words and same order, with no other speaker between them. The list gives 'everything' its referent in the same panel. The register stack, ringing phone and queue are kept as props and staging. Artwork note: speaking mid-call must read as a sigh aside.

Ananya's 'Our time belongs with patients. Let's make the rest simpler.' matches source P1-3 verbatim. Read from the comic alone, 'the rest' means the 01-2 paperwork set against patient time, and her gaze is on the desk, as in the source ('looks thoughtfully at the reception desk'). This is the motive for page 2.

Caption 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.' matches source P2-1 verbatim and carries the time and place jump. The label 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic' is an addition naming the product the source puts on the laptop ('laptop view of Welbuk Practice'); it fixes Practice = clinic. Generic blank fields meet 'non-sensitive setup fields'. The evening setting is recorded as a supplement.

Ananya's 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.' matches source P2-2 verbatim. 'Here' refers to the 02-1 laptop and the Practice label. The scene keeps 'enters clinic information and considers team roles', which sets up Meera's staff-role line.

Meera's 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.' matches source P2-3 verbatim. Its 'And' continues Ananya's 02-2 line directly, with no speech removed in between. The label 'WELBUK CARE for clinic staff' names the source's staff app and fixes Care = staff. The staff phone is in Meera's right hand, consistent with hands and props.

Ananya's 'One team. Better coordination.' matches source P2-4 verbatim and sums up 02-2 (clinic) and 02-3 (staff). Meera nods silently, consistent with 'friendly two-shot'. The staff phone stays in Meera's right hand, matching 02-3.

Ravi's 'Good morning! I'd like to see the doctor.' matches source P3-1 verbatim and needs no earlier context. There is no transition caption, as in the source. The later morning and the tidy desk with monitor are supplements the art must show. The shoulder bag is introduced, held in his left hand while he waves with his right.

Meera's 'Of course. May I register your details for today's appointment?' matches source P3-2 verbatim. 'Of course' answers the 03-1 request, and she asks for consent before any data entry, as the source requires ('asks for consent to collect the information needed').

Ravi's 'Yes, please.' matches source P3-3 verbatim and directly answers the 03-2 question, so the question keeps its answer. The monitor shows only blank fields and there are no papers or ID cards, which satisfies 'no actual identifying data'.

Meera's 'You're all set, Ravi. Please have a seat.' matches source P3-4 verbatim. 'All set' follows the 03-3 data entry, and she knows his name from registration. 'Have a seat' sets up the wait before 04-1.

Her open question is answered in 04-2. The closed laptop pushed aside supports the page's theme. Artwork note: Ravi's shoulder bag is no longer recorded.
Ravi's 'I've been feeling tired lately.' matches source P4-2 verbatim and answers the 04-1 question directly. It is a routine concern; no diagnosis or advice appears, as the source requires.
